subject: Streaming pipeline & connection capacity for AstraPay integration
messages:
From: Charlotte Lee <charlotte@astrapay.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Cc: AstraPay Platform Team <ops@astrapay.com>
Date: Sun, 1 Jul 2028 12:09:00 -0700
Subject: AstraPay integration — post-demo throughput & latency targets

Kimberly,

Thanks again for the demo today — the streaming demo hit a lot of our engineering checkboxes. Per our call, sharing a concise recap of what we're trying to achieve and a few hard requirements from the platform side so you can advise on limits/quota. Attached is a short spreadsheet with sample traffic patterns. Key points: 

- Workload: real-time transaction enrichment + short transcripts (streaming chunks).
- Expected steady concurrency: 800–1,200 simultaneous user streams during peak.
- Burst events: up to 2,400 concurrent streams for 30–90s during payroll windows.
- Average tokens per second per stream: ~6–10 (mostly short chunks) — estimate ~9 TPS.
- Aggregate request profile: ~10–20 requests/sec for non-stream RPCs; streaming is the bulk.
- Latency expectation: 95th <= 150ms per chunk for streaming responses; tail matters since UX degrades quickly.

Questions for you:
1) What connection model and per-customer quotas would Redwood recommend for 1k sustained streams under our latency target?
2) How do rate limits behave for streaming vs non-stream calls? Any separate quota or shared token pool?
3) Can Redwood support long-lived multiplexed connections (HTTP/2 or HTTP/3) with multiple concurrent streams per connection?
4) How does prefix/KV caching interact with streaming latencies — can we keep warm-state per user?
5) Any suggested fallback model variants (lower-cost) for graceful degradation when capacity is constrained?

If you can sketch a recommended quota/burst profile and an initial cost ballpark, that would help our procurement team.

Thanks,
Charlotte
Director of Platform Engineering
AstraPay

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Charlotte Lee <charlotte@astrapay.com>

Subject: Re: AstraPay integration — post-demo throughput & latency targets

Kimberly / Charlotte — digging into the spreadsheet. High-level feasibility: this is achievable on hosted Redwood with careful connection/pooling config and an agreed quota profile. Below are my recommendations and caveats.

Recommended connection & pooling model:
- Use long-lived HTTP/2 connections (or HTTP/3 where available) with multiplexing. Aim for ~6 concurrent streams per TCP connection to balance head-of-line issues and OS/TCP limits.
- Client architecture: maintain a small connection pool per client process (3–8 connections) and multiplex sessions inside. This reduces TCP churn and TLS handshakes.
- Edge placement: route clients to the nearest Redwood edge region; we can pin AstraPay to US-West for lower tail latency.

Quota & rate limit proposal (hosted):
- Per-customer sustained token allowance: 25,000 tokens/sec (estimate covers 1k streams * 9 TPS * buffer for control calls).
- Burst window: allow bursts up to 60,000 tokens/sec for up to 90s with an exponential backoff policy.
- Concurrent streaming session soft quota: 2,500 concurrent streams (soft limit with priority queueing).
- Connection limit guidance: no more than 3,000 concurrent HTTP/2 connections from a single ASN to a Redwood edge to avoid upstream NAT exhaustion.

Streaming vs non-streaming behavior:
- Streaming consumes tokens as chunks are produced; those tokens count against the same token pool as non-stream calls by default. We can create a separate streaming pool if AstraPay prefers isolated quotas (recommended for predictable QoS).
- Streaming uses persistent KV cache pinning where feasible — we can keep warm per-session state (prefix cache) for active streams, but cold-starts will incur extra latency.

Fallback strategy:
- Primary model: L2-latency-optimized variant (meets 95th ~140–160ms for short chunks).
- Degradation: when token pool is exhausted, route to lower-cost L3 variant with longer latency and reduced context window; preserve graceful partial responses with explicit "degraded" flag in metadata.

Operational & observability notes:
- We provide token-level breakdown, per-route SLA dashboards, and per-session trace IDs to correlate spikes with user cohorts.
- We'll add a throttling alert/notification for AstraPay when aggregate sustained tokens exceed 80% of allocated quota.

Preliminary cost outline (hosted pilot):
- Pilot configuration (30 days): rate-limited plan with 25k sustained tokens/sec + burst headroom — estimated hosted spend: ~$65k–$95k for the pilot depending on chunk sizes and duration.

I'll attach a quick architecture diagram and a CSV of simulated token burn for the patterns in your spreadsheet. If AstraPay is comfortable, we can spin up a short pilot and instrument the workloads.

Rishi
Infra Lead, Redwood Inference

- For bursts: 90s headroom is fine, but we need a hard safety mechanism so our UX degrades predictably (rate-limited vs dropped).
- Can you provide a short JSON example of the degraded response payload (so our client-side code can handle it)?
- Procurement ask: a one-page pilot agreement + PO-ready pricing that quotes the 30-day trial estimate and clear overage rates.

We're ok to schedule a technical handoff call this week (Thu or Fri PST). If you can send a calendar invite I'll accept.

—Charlotte
